title: China’s Military Is Now Using AI to Plan Strike Operations
gist: A CCTV documentary marking the PLA's 99th anniversary revealed, without fanfare, that the PLA Air Force is already operating an AI system that prioritizes targets from a pool of hundreds, coordinates dozens of formations, and tasks more than 100 tactical units — aligning with Xi Jinping's late-July push for intelligent military systems ahead of the 2027 modernization milestone.

insights.claim: The PLA Air Force now uses an AI system that draws up plans for large-scale strike operations, prioritizing targets from a pool of hundreds, coordinating dozens of formations, and assigning tasks to more than 100 tactical units.
insights.speaker: Gerald Mako
insights.so_what: AI has moved from Chinese military rhetoric to campaign-level planning at scale, compressing decision cycles in any Taiwan or South China Sea contingency.
insights.quote: The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force now uses an AI system that draws up plans for large-scale strike operations.

insights.claim: According to the CCTV documentary, the PLA's AI strike-planning system has already been used in multiple missions, meaning it is fielded rather than experimental.
insights.speaker: Gerald Mako
insights.so_what: Deployed-and-used status shortens the assumed timeline for AI-enabled Chinese military capability that Western planning has treated as future-tense.
insights.quote: According to the documentary, it has already been used in multiple missions.

insights.claim: The system was disclosed quietly inside a CCTV documentary marking the PLA's 99th anniversary rather than through a fanfare announcement, suggesting Beijing is normalizing AI-enabled command capability rather than signaling it.
insights.speaker: Gerald Mako
insights.so_what: Low-key disclosure channels mean state media documentaries are an underrated intelligence source for tracking PLA capability milestones.
insights.quote: Instead of being released with great fanfare, the system appeared in a CCTV documentary released in early August
insights.locator: Instead of being released with great fanfare

insights.claim: Xi Jinping instructed in late July that the PLA must strengthen the military application of unmanned intelligent technologies and gradually build an intelligent military system — a goal China has pursued for years, so the news is the elevated level of emphasis rather than the objective itself.
insights.speaker: Gerald Mako
insights.so_what: Read escalating emphasis, not novelty, as the signal — rising rhetorical priority typically precedes budget and procurement reallocation.
insights.quote: As China has been pursuing this very goal for years, Xi’s remarks are not new. The level of emphasis, however, is high
insights.locator: The timing lines up neatly with Xi Jinping’s instruction

insights.claim: Beijing wants steady progress toward PLA modernization goals set for 2027, the 100th anniversary of the PLA's founding, giving the AI-enabled command push a hard political deadline.
insights.speaker: Gerald Mako
insights.so_what: 2027 is the date to anchor capability-milestone expectations and regional risk premia in defense, semiconductors, and Taiwan-exposed supply chains.
